Classical Latin length distinction becomes a quality (tense) distinction, first pass
posttonic ʊ/o syncopates before l + vowel near the end of the word
lax high vowels lower to tense mid vowels
word-final nasal consonant lost after an unstressed vowel
a stressed vowel lengthens before a plosive + non-nasal sonorant (muta cum liquida)
a velar stop spirantizes after a vowel/glide before a coronal consonant
a vowel shortens before a consonant cluster
the back high continuant obstruent (x) fronts before a coronal
a lateral palatalizes after a high-front consonant
short stressed ɛ/ɔ also diphthongize before a high-front consonant
yod lost before ʎ or palatalized r
an unstressed non-low non-nasalized vowel reduces to schwa before a consonant or word end
schwa becomes non-syllabic
non-syllabic schwa is lost elsewhere
a high tense round non-nasal vowel centralizes (recurrence)
high round back vowels front (completion of u-fronting)
the diphthong uo becomes ue
the stressed diphthong ye̯ (from ue̯) monophthongizes to ø
front round ø opens to œ before a coda consonant in the final syllable
stress is leveled — no longer distinctive
ʎ becomes j
